audience: Two-to-five engineer product team shipping their first AI feature
production_audience: Product engineering team operating multiple AI agents across providers in production, with past incidents and weekly per-agent cost reporting
observed_email:
You already call the model. That was never the hard part

Preview: The endpoint, the spend ceiling and the run record are what took the incidents to build.

The line your CSV export does not have

Hi there,

Someone asks what the AI feature cost last week, and on which model. Answering means writing a reporting job first.

So it becomes the provider dashboards, one tab each, and an export lined up by hand. The total comes out. The line that says which agent caused it does not.

The retry loop, the session table, the spend sheet — each got built after the incident that proved it was missing. And usage keyed to whoever holds the provider key can tell you who spent, not which agent spent.

orqAgent is a hosted layer where an agent is a configuration object — system prompt, model, knowledge base, guardrails — with its own REST endpoint and API key auth. The ceiling is a field on the key, not middleware you write.

Every call through that endpoint is recorded with its tokens, latency and model, tracked without extra config. Calling the provider SDK directly still gets you the model. It does not get you the cap or the run record.

Create one agent, call its endpoint once, then read the run.

Create your first agent →

* the orqAgent team

P.S. The free plan needs no card. One agent is enough to test this.

adapted_body:
Hi there,

As you prepare your first AI feature, you may want a way to inspect a call before deciding how to operate it.

orqAgent is a hosted layer for configuring an agent and calling its REST endpoint with API key authentication. Calls through that endpoint record tokens, latency and model; a spending ceiling can be set on the key.

If that fits what you are preparing, create one agent, call its endpoint and inspect the recorded run.

The orqAgent team
